purpose: Test on a fourth non-overlapping time sample whether one scalar power offset frozen entirely from the prior 06:00 UTC stability result collapses H10S2 toward H10N1 simultaneously across time and across fixed 10-80 Hz subbands, without fitting or recentering on the holdout.

frozen_scalar.definition: Subtract this exact power-ratio offset from every holdout S2-minus-N1 dB ratio; equivalently multiply H10S2 waveform amplitude by the fixed amplitude factor before PSD estimation.
frozen_scalar.source_statistic: prior 06:00 UTC response-corrected median S2-minus-N1 10-80 Hz power ratio

holdout_window_contract.independence_from_prior_samples: The 18:00 UTC holdout windows do not overlap the prior 00:00, 06:00, or 12:00 baseline samples.

per_complete_window: uncollapsed raw and response-corrected S2-minus-N1 10-80 Hz power-ratio dB
collapsed raw and response-corrected residual dB after subtracting the one frozen scalar
aggregate_broadband: fraction of complete windows with absolute raw residual <= 3 dB
fraction of complete windows with absolute corrected residual <= 3 dB
fraction with both absolute residuals <= 3 dB
aggregate_fixed_subbands: median collapsed raw residual dB in each frozen subband
median collapsed corrected residual dB in each frozen subband

classification_thresholds.engineering_interpretation: PASS requires the single frozen scalar to generalize without refitting: broadband residual medians near zero, limited temporal dispersion, at least 80% of paired windows within ±3 dB in both raw and corrected power, and all predeclared subband residual medians within ±2.5 dB. These are morphology/generalization criteria only, not causal-identification criteria.

claim_ceiling: A PASS establishes only that one scalar offset frozen from the prior 06:00 UTC result predicts and approximately collapses the H10S2-over-H10N1 broadband power difference on a new 18:00 UTC holdout, including the three fixed subbands. This would support a persistent multiplicative station-path factor as a compact description, but would not identify sensor gain, calibration, site, deployment, or environmental cause. A FAIL means the one-scalar description does not generalize under these frozen tolerances; it does not erase earlier replicated asymmetry findings. Neither outcome validates 119 Hz or changes target identity.
